title: Father's trade and relatives not in music
summary: Father was a shoemaker with a repair and coal shop in the district; grandparents and uncles did not play music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I don't like to keep harping about the family, but the farther back we can go naturally, the better we like this older material. Did any of your other relatives, any uncles, did your father have any brothers or anyone else in his family that played music? Oh, yeah. Did you knew of him?
I know one of his brothers was a mattress maker. I think his brother was a little older than him. Then he had two other brothers.
Did your father have any other trade or did he just? He was a shoemaker. Shoemaker.

He used to make shoes. Then he opened up a shoe repair shop and he had a wooden coal shop right in the red light district. He used to serve all the district with coal in the winter time. His place was right here on Murray between Coddye and St. Louis. And he was there for many, many years before I was born until he died. I was a boy about 13. He was still there. That's when his place closed up when he died. Because my brothers and them didn't fool with nothing like that. They had got to be young men and they didn't want that kind of business.
Do you remember, did your grandfather, did you ever remember your grandfather? No, I don't remember my... Or did they play any instruments?

No, I don't think they played any instruments. I never heard of them. Honestly, what I can remember is my grandmother. My daddy's mother, I remembered her. Well, she died when I must have been about eight or nine years old. I remember going to her and seeing her and all, but I don't know too much about her. But as far as his daddy, he died before I was born. But he did have two brothers.
Besides, the one I'm telling you was the mattress maker. They were older than him and this brother, but I don't know anything about them.

No, I don't know anything about them. I don't think they played any music. I never heard anybody say nothing about them playing music. But through the line, through the family of my side, I can remember up until my brother Sidney, it looked like we all went out, the music went out of the family until recently years. I have a nephew came up. My sister's son, well he's a cracker jack sax player. But that's late stuff. That's late stuff.
